Term1: Neutropenic fever--patient is a candidate for oral therapy
Text:
# NEUTROPENIC FEVER--PATIENT IS A CANDIDATE FOR ORAL THERAPY

## Can the patient be treated with oral therapy?

[Link to a scoring tool that identifies low risk patients for oral therapy](febrile-neutropenia-scoring-tool)
References:

- Freifeld AG Clinical Infectious Disease 2011, 52: 427-431
- Taplitz RA, J Clin Oncol 2018, 36: 1443-1453
- Sanford: Neutropenia, Febrile, Low-Risk
- NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines, Prevention and Treatment of Cancer-
- Related Infections. Version 1.2019. nccn.org
Therapy:
Ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO q12h ($) [R,DI] <AND> amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg PO q12h ($) [R]
Alternative:
Ciprofloxacin 500mg PO q12h ($) [R,DI] <AND> Clindamycin 300mg po q6h ($) [H,O]
Inpt: ORZID2 GMENU NEUT FEVER CAND ORAL THERA
Outpt: ORZID3 GMENU NEUT CAND ORAL THERAPY
